verdict.h: A bigger season in dollars, flat in orders, and dearer to advertise
verdict.b: We expect US online holiday spend up about 7% and Cyber Week up about 7%, but orders up only 1 to 3%: the growth is price, mix and a busier five days, not more shoppers. Meta will cost roughly 18% more than last BFCM and spike about 60% from early November to Black Friday, while Google clicks get only about 4% dearer. The median brand will launch around Nov 12 and apparel around Nov 14, with the biggest launch day on Friday Nov 20. Canada stays soft. Overall: a strong November and December for revenue, an average one for margin.

items.m: US online holiday spend, Nov to Dec
items.basis: Adobe forecasts +6.7% ($275.1B), Bain sees non-store +9% and Mastercard online +11%. Shoppers are gloomy (sentiment 48.0, 35% trading down), so we sit near Adobe rather than the top of the range.

items.m: US Cyber Week online spend (Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday)
items.basis: Adobe $47.5B (+7.4%); Bain expects the BFCM weekend to grow +8.75%, nearly twice the season. More of the season's growth lands on the five days.

items.call: Orders +1% to +3%; revenue up mainly on price and AOV
items.basis: Last year US orders grew 1% while spend grew on price. Bain and Mastercard both say about half of this year's growth is inflation, and 35% of shoppers are trading down.
Adobe forecasts apparel +4.7% against +6.7% overall, and apparel peaks at 23% off on Black Friday, no deeper than 2025. Expect apparel to lean on volume and Black Friday itself.

items.m: Meta CPM during BFCM vs BFCM 2025
items.basis: Northbeam's weekly Meta CPM is running about 25% above last year in October; Meta's own price per ad rose 14% worldwide and 23% in the US and Canada in Q3. We shade it below the October gap because last year's BFCM already carried a large peak premium.

items.m: Meta CPM spike: Black Friday vs early November
items.call: about +60% vs the first week of November
items.basis: Howland's accounts saw Black Friday day-one CPMs 45% above the week before; Lebesgue saw +84% against September; Common Thread's brands paid 26% more in November than October.

items.m: Google Search cost per click, Q4 YoY
items.basis: Alphabet's cost per click rose 5%, 3% and 4% in the first three quarters of 2026 while paid clicks grew 8 to 13%. Search stays far cheaper to scale than Meta this peak.

items.m: Median brand's first Black Friday ad
items.basis: Same 13 days out lands on Nov 14. Demand is pulling forward (71% plan to buy before Black Friday, Adobe October +8%, 22% starting earlier) and Amazon is expected to start around Nov 19, so we expect brands a couple of days earlier.

items.m: Apparel & footwear: median brand's first Black Friday ad
items.basis: Apparel launched two days later than all brands last year; same gap on our all-brand call. 9% of apparel brands were live by Nov 1 against 12.5% overall.
1 in 5 brands ran early access a median 17 days out; 26.5% of apparel brands did. We expect slightly more early access this year (about 22% of brands, 28% in apparel) given the early-demand signals.

items.m: Biggest launch day for full Black Friday sales
items.basis: Last year's peak was the Friday before Black Friday, followed by Thanksgiving and Black Friday itself. The calendar repeats one day earlier.

items.m: Brands making separate Cyber Monday creative
items.basis: Cyber Monday intent is up (Bain 44% from 41% in the US; RCC 72% from 64% in Canada). About 60% of those will keep their Black Friday number, as 61% did.

items.m: Median days a Black Friday ad stays live
items.basis: Run length barely moves by brand size or offer. The median brand's campaign runs about 18 days from first ad (Nov 12) to Cyber Monday (Nov 30); about 12% will add new ads Dec 1 to 6, mostly gifting copy.

items.m: Median discount named in Black Friday ads
items.basis: 50% was the median in every follower band and in most categories (sports and outdoor 40%); 60% of marketers say they'll hold discount depth. Adobe's actual price cuts peak at about 30% in Cyber Week.

items.call: Flat to slightly down overall; Black Friday holds
items.basis: Budgets are down (RCC -6.5% to $911; Deloitte -14% to $1,305), but 88% rank Black Friday in their top three days and 42% of budgets go online.
